To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the glycosylation of GPA-M and -N differentially modulates antigenic properties of the peptide and that some anti-M MoAbs cross-react with variant Mg erythrocyte antigen.

(1) glycosylation of the amino acid residue adjacent to the most essential part of peptidine epitope can modulate the proper exposure of the epitope; and (2) glycosylation can also modulate the epitope recognition by MoAb.

1) the glycosylated and nonglycosylated variants of GPA-M differ in the reactivity with some MoAbs, 2) the glycosylation-dependent differences in reactivity are due to the changes in the antigenicity of peptide backbone, and 3) the glycosidic moiety of GPA-M may be considered as an integral part of blood group M-related peptidic determinant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of blood group antigens.
the analysis of epitope structures and antigen-antibody interactions.
the influence of glycosylation of GPA on its recognition by anti-GPA MoAbs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glycosylation may modulate antigenicity of protein by changing the structure or the exposure of peptide epitopes.

the MoAbs 425/2A, 425/3B, and 425/2C are specific for blood group M-related peptidic determinant in which Met8 is the most important amino acid residue, whereas Met8, Val6, and Gly5 are the most important amino acids for MoAbs E3, E6 (425/2B), and 425/3C, respectively.
the glycosylation of GPA-Mg, which differs from that of GPA-M/N, results in the exposure of peptic epitope recognized by anti-M/Mg antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anti-M/Mg monoclonal antibodies described here are not specific for M- or N-type epitope but for M-related epitope, and that glycosylation modulates the antigenic properties of the epitope.
the glycosylation of GPA is a critical factor in the proper expression of blood group M-related antigenic epitope.
the MoAbs directed to the peptidic portion of GPA-M epitope recognize only the nonglycosylated form of the epitope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glycosylation can alter antigenicity in a number of ways, including masking or unmasking of epitopes.
the presence or absence of O-linked sialoligosaccharides at Ser2, Thr2, and Thr3 residues of the N-terminal portion GPA-M or -Mg may be used for the differentiation between GPA-M and GPA-Mg.
glycosylation is not only a modulator of antigenic properties, but it can be also a modulator of epitope structure.
